newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A steady supply of dollars to the South African currency market saw the rand push to a new seven-and-a-half week high on Wednesday while long bonds pierced key technical levels to trade at new three-month highs.
The rand closed at 4.6300/6350 on a strong dollar after reaching a new 7-1/2 week high during the morning and from 4.6520/6570 at Tuesday's close.
Forex traders pinpointed favourable rand sentiment out of Europe and offshore dollar sales -- mainly out of London -- as the two factors behind the unit's gains.

"Sentiment seems to have changed in Europe...for the last two to three weeks we've seen constant dollar sales and it looks like there's a favourable discount for investing in the rand," a trader at one of the country's four leading banks said.
This view was echoed by other traders who said the currency had also been supported by a stronger bond market.
Looking at the technical picture, UAL Merchant Bank Treasury financial market analyst Boyd Stafne said new levels to look at against the dollar were around 4.6000 to 4.6050.
But he sounded a warning that the currency's most recent strength could be short-lived.
"It's a good sign but it's early days and let's not be widely euphoric yet," Stafne said.

Forex traders said news that the South African cabinet had deferred a decision on a controversial but lucrative arms sale to Syria to a future meeting had been received well offshore and saw the rand firm briefly.
One said the 4.6250 level was key to watch on Thursday and another assault on the downside was possible as offshore banks were still keen to sell the U.S. unit.

On the crosses, the rand swept to a new six-month high on the mark to last trade at 0.3535/3540 from 0.3486/3490 previously. Against sterling it was at a six-week high, last trading at 7.6744/6873 from 7.7519/7649.

Long bonds held below the crucial 15.50 percent level after piercing the figure in early trade on generally upbeat comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan -- which helped the U.S. market -- and a strong rand.
Government's benchmark R150 stock last yielded 15.49 percent from 15.63 percent after a new three-month high of 15.465 percent during the morning.
"The market strengthened on technical buying with quite a few players looking to pick up stock at the 15.50 percent level," a bond trader commented.
UAL's Stafne said more strength to around the 15.40/15.41 percent levels was possible.

"At about 15.40 percent the bond market would have gone a long way in a fairly short while and may be a little overbought," he said, noting that the market had not yet had a decent retracement since it started strengthening at the start of the year.
Other traders said U.S. rates would be key in determining direction on Thursday and the market was also awaiting the release of December trade figures -- due out from Thursday.
Foreigners sold a net 42.32 million rands' worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 74.33 million on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 4.81 billion rand on Tuesday from Monday's 4.03 billion rand, it said.
The Reserve Bank said South Africa's money market shortage rose to 10.664 billion rand on Tuesday from Monday's 10.446 billion rand.
However, leading banks continued to quote their three-month NCD rates steady at between 17.25-17.50 percent while 90-day BA rates were also unchanged at 16.60-16.85 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
